title: Festivals & vrats
noneThisDay: No festival or vrat on this day.
remindDenied: Notifications are off for Astropedia. Turn them on in your phone's settings to get reminders.
approxNote: Dates follow the {{city}} sunrise and the usual North Indian rules, so they're approximate. Your family or region may keep a festival or vrat a day apart; both are fine.

short.navratri: nine nights of the Goddess begin

about.purnima: Full moon day. Many keep a light fast, read the Satyanarayan katha or simply spend a quiet evening with family.
about.amavasya: New moon day. A day to remember ancestors, rest and keep things simple.
about.pradosh-shukla: Trayodashi evening, kept for Shiva. A light fast and prayer around sunset.
about.pradosh-krishna: Trayodashi evening, kept for Shiva. A light fast and prayer around sunset.
about.sankashti: Kept for Ganesha. Many fast through the day and break it after seeing the moon rise.
about.maha-shivaratri: The great night of Shiva. Many fast and stay up through the night with prayer.
about.holika-dahan: The bonfire on the evening of Phalguna Purnima, the good burning away the bad.
about.holi: The festival of colours, the morning after Holika Dahan.
about.ram-navami: Rama's birthday, celebrated at midday with prayer and stories of the Ramayana.
about.hanuman-jayanti: Hanuman's birthday on Chaitra Purnima (in North India). The Hanuman Chalisa is often recited.
about.raksha-bandhan: Sisters tie a rakhi on their brothers' wrists, and brothers promise to look out for them.
about.janmashtami: Krishna's birthday. Many fast until midnight, when he was born.
about.ganesh-chaturthi: Ganesha is welcomed home for a few days of prayer and sweets.
about.mahalaya: The last day of Pitru Paksha. Tarpan for ancestors in the morning; in Bengal, the start of Devi Paksha.
about.navratri: Nine nights of the Goddess begin. Ghatasthapana is best in the morning, after sunrise and outside Rahu Kaal.
about.durga-saptami: The first big day of Durga Puja: Nabapatrika snan at dawn, then pandal visits.
about.durga-ashtami: Many fast until the Sandhi Puja. Kumari Puja is held in the morning.
about.durga-navami: The last full day of Puja, ending with the Navami bhog.
about.bijoya-dashami: Durga's farewell: sindoor khela, immersion and Bijoya greetings.
about.dussehra: Good over evil. One of the best days of the year to begin something new.
about.kojagari: Full moon night for Lakshmi. Keep a lamp lit and stay awake a while.
about.karva-chauth: A fast for a partner's long life, broken after seeing the moon.
about.dhanteras: The first day of Diwali. A small purchase for the home, and a lamp for Yama in the evening.
about.diwali: Lakshmi Puja in the evening, lamps everywhere, sweets and family.
about.kali-puja: In Bengal, Kali Puja is held through the night of Diwali's new moon.
about.bhai-dooj: Sisters pray for their brothers, who visit and share a meal.
about.chhath: Prayers to the setting and rising Sun, kept with great care, especially in Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh.
about.makar-sankranti: The Sun moves into Capricorn: til-gud, kites and a holy dip.
about.poila-boishakh: The first day of the Bengali year: new clothes, Haal Khata and sweets.
about.ekadashi: The eleventh lunar day, kept for Vishnu. Many skip grains from sunrise to the next morning.
about.ekadashiAdhika: An Ekadashi of the extra (adhika) month, which comes about every three years. Kept like any Ekadashi.
